raw_text:
Below is a 12-week, clinic-to-ski safe strength program you can run with this client. It respects the surgeon’s restrictions (no jumping, no deep knee flexion under load) while building strength, unilateral control and ski-specific force transfer. Plan format: phases, 4 training sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B), weeks by week with sets/reps, tempo and progression rules, warm-up/cool-down, recovery and nutrition guidance, and safety/progression checkpoints.

Key constraints and coaching notes (apply every session)
- No loaded knee flexion past roughly 90° (avoid “below parallel” deep squats). Use boxes/markers to limit depth. If you want a precise target, stop at ~60–90° knee angle depending on pain — conservative = ~70–80°.
- No jumping or high-impact plyometrics.
- Watch for swelling/effusion after sessions. If increased swelling or pain >4/10, back off volume/intensity and consult physio/surgeon.
- Emphasize controlled eccentrics, good hip hinge, and single‑leg balance/strength to address asymmetry from the meniscal repair.
- Use RPE/autoregulation: if movement quality or pain degrades, reduce load or reps.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B). Optional 1–2 low-impact conditioning sessions (bike/elliptical) on off days.
- Phases: Foundation/Reconditioning (Weeks 1–4), Strength Build (Weeks 5–8), Strength + Power Transfer (Weeks 9–12).
- Deloads: Week 4 and Week 8 are lighter (reduce volume by ~30–40%, keep intensity moderate). These are built into the plan.
- Progression: Weeks 1–3 increase load/volume gradually (add 2.5–5% load or 1–2 reps per set where appropriate). Weeks 5–7 increase intensity (heavier, lower reps). Weeks 9–12 increase intensity with more velocity/force work (sleds, explosive concentric only). Use conservative progression given surgical history.

Warm-up (do before each session, 10–15 minutes)
1. 5–8 min low-impact cardio (bike or elliptical).
2. Dynamic mobility: ankle dorsiflexion drills, hip CARs, thoracic rotations, cat-cow.
3. Knee/glute activation (2 sets each, light): quad sets, mini band lateral walks (2 x 10–15m), clamshells 2x12 each side, single-leg balance 2x30s.
4. Warm-up sets for main lifts (2–3 progressively heavier sets x 5–8 reps).

Cool-down (5–10 minutes)
- Light bike 3–5 min, foam rolling quads/glutes/hamstrings, gentle quad/hamstring/hip flexor stretches. If postoperative swelling occurs after session, 10–15 minutes icing and elevation may be helpful.

Session tempo/rest guidance
- Tempo notation: eccentric-pause-concentric (e.g., 3-1-1 = 3s down, 1s pause, explode up). Use slower eccentrics (2–4s) early in phases to build control.
- Rest: main lifts 2–3 min; accessory 60–90s; single-leg and core 60s.

Phase 1 — Foundation & Reconditioning (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: restore movement quality, unilateral strength, build base hypertrophy and tolerance to load without deep knee flexion. Focus on controlled eccentrics and hip-dominant patterns.

Week 1 (start conservative)
Upper A
1. Bench press — 3 x 6–8 (tempo 2-0-1) Rest 2 min
2. Bent-over DB row or chest-supported row — 3 x 8–10
3. Seated DB overhead press — 3 x 8–10
4. Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up — 3 x 8–10
5. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
6. Farmers carry 3 x 40–60s (core/upper back)

Lower A
1. Trap-bar deadlift — 3 x 6–8 (3s down, controlled) Rest 2–3 min
2. Box squat (box height set to avoid >90° knee flexion) — 3 x 6–8 (2-1-1)
3. Single-leg RDL (light DB) — 3 x 8 each leg (2s eccentric)
4. Glute bridge (barbell or banded) — 3 x 8–12
5. Lying leg curl — 3 x 10–12
6. Pallof press — 3 x 10 each side

Upper B
1. Incline DB press — 3 x 6–8
2. Single-arm row — 3 x 8–10 each
3. Arnold/DB press or seated press — 3 x 8–10
4. Cable face pull — 3 x 12–15
5. Biceps curls + triceps pushdown superset — 3 x 10–12

Lower B
1. Sled push (light to moderate) — 6 x 20–30 m (low impact power)
2. Reverse lunge to partial depth (stop before deep knee flexion) — 3 x 8 each leg
3. Leg press (partial ROM to ~90° knee flexion max) — 3 x 10–12
4. Standing single-leg calf raise — 3 x 12–15 each
5. Side-lying hip abduction or banded lateral walks — 3 x 12–15
6. Bird dog — 3 x 8 each side

Weeks 2–3
- Increase weight modestly on main lifts (add 2.5–5% or 1–2 reps).
- Keep sets similar; emphasize technique and control.
- Optional: add 1 low-impact cardio session (30 min bike) midweek.

Week 4 — Deload
- Reduce sets by ~30–40% (e.g., main lifts 2 x 6–8 at ~60–70% load), reduce accessory volume. Keep movement patterns but lower intensity. Use this week to check knee response and adjust box heights/step heights.

Phase 2 — Strength Build (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase maximal strength, maintain joint safety. Shift to heavier loads, lower reps on primary lifts; keep single-leg work and eccentric control.

Week 5 (restart after deload)
Upper A
1. Bench press — 4 x 5–6 (RPE 7–8)
2. Bent-over row — 4 x 6–8
3. Seated DB press — 3 x 6–8
4. Weighted chin-up or lat pulldown — 3 x 6–8
5. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15

Lower A
1. Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 4–6 (heavier; focus on hip drive) Rest 2–3 min
2. Box squat — 4 x 4–6 (box height unchanged)
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 6–8 each leg (use short ROM — stop before deep flexion)
4. Glute bridge or hip thrust — 3 x 6–8 (heavier)
5. Hamstring curl — 3 x 8–10
6. Anti-rotation cable hold (Pallof) — 3 x 8–10 each side

Upper B
1. Overhead press (barbell or DB) — 4 x 5–6
2. Single-arm row or T-bar row — 4 x 6–8
3. Incline DB press — 3 x 6–8
4. Rear-delt fly / face pull — 3 x 12–15
5. Farmer carry / suitcase carry — 3 rounds

Lower B
1. Sled push/pull — 6–8 x 20–30 m (increase load slightly for force)
2. Partial range front squat to box (or goblet box squat) — 3 x 6–8 (NO deep flexion)
3. Single-leg RDL heavy — 3 x 6–8 each leg
4. Leg curl (Nordic assisted or machine) — 3 x 6–8
5. Lateral band walks — 3 x 15

Weeks 6–7
- Add load on main lifts as tolerated; aim for gradual increase in set intensity.
- Keep single-leg work heavy enough to correct imbalances but watch knee symptoms.
- Keep sled sessions to maintain low-impact power transfer.

Week 8 — Deload
- Reduce volume by ~30–40% again. Maintain technique work and test single-leg balance and control. If swelling/pain persists, extend deload for another week or reduce volume again.

Phase 3 — Strength → Power Transfer for Skiing (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: convert strength into high-rate-of-force production and eccentric control needed for skiing. No jumps — use sleds, medicine-ball throws, isometric holds, heavy eccentrics and fast concentric-only actions on machines.

Week 9
Upper A
1. Bench press — 4 x 3–5 (heavier, RPE 8)
2. Weighted pull-up or heavy lat pulldown — 4 x 4–6
3. Seated DB press — 3 x 5–6
4. Single-arm row — 3 x 6
5. Med-ball chest pass (explode concentric) — 3 x 6–8

Lower A
1. Trap-bar deadlift — 4 x 3–5 (heavier)
2. Box squat — 4 x 3–5 (safe depth) focus on fast concentric
3. Heavy single-leg RDL — 3 x 5–6
4. Hip thrust (slow eccentric, explosive concentric) — 3 x 5–6
5. Sled push heavy (force) — 6 x 20 m (short rest)

Upper B
1. Incline bench heavy — 4 x 4–6
2. Bent-over row heavy — 4 x 4–6
3. Overhead single-arm press — 3 x 5–6
4. Core anti-rotation throws (cable or medball) — 3 x 8 each

Lower B
1. Step-downs (eccentric-focused) — 4 x 6–8 each (low step; slow controlled descent)
2. Leg press heavy partial ROM — 4 x 6–8
3. Lying hamstring curl (eccentric emphasis) — 3 x 6–8
4. Lateral loaded carry or sled lateral push — 3 x 30 m
5. Calf raises heavy — 4 x 8–10

Week 10–11
- Maintain heavy main lifts (3–5 reps), but incorporate more explosive concentric intent (e.g., push as fast as possible while maintaining control).
- Increase sled loads and reduce push distance for maximal force.
- Do one session per week with heavier eccentric emphasis (4s lowering) on a key lift to improve eccentric control for carving/edge control.

Week 12 — Peak & Testing (keep it aggressive but safe)
- Reduce accessory volume; perform main lifts at planned heavier loads for 3–4 sets of 3–4 reps. Example:
  - Trap bar or deadlift 4 x 3 at 90% of recent 3RM (only if movement quality perfect).
  - Box squats 4 x 3 (same safety).
- Complete ski-specific test: single-leg hold/step down control, 3x timed heavy sled pushes, core anti-rotation strength. Don’t max out if swelling appears.
- Finish with mobility and plan transition to on-snow conditioning (after clearance).

Optional conditioning (2x week, on non-lifting days)
- Low-impact steady-state cardio: 25–45 min bike/elliptical at moderate effort.
- Intervals on bike: 6–8 x 60s high effort / 90s easy.
- Ski-specific: ski-erg if available (low impact), building 10–20 min intervals.

Knee-specific rehab & mobility (ongoing)
- Continue glute medius and VMO activation: banded side steps, clamshells, straight-leg raises.
- Improve ankle dorsiflexion (affects squat depth and knee mechanics).
- Manual therapy or regular physio sessions if available (once every 1–4 weeks depending on needs).
- Controlled step-down progressions: start low step, increase height gradually if pain-free.

Progression rules & return-to-ski checkpoints
- Progress load only if: no new swelling, pain ≤ 3/10 during activity and resolving quickly after, ROM stable.
- Strength symmetry goal: aim for <10–15% unilateral asymmetry in single-leg RDL/leg press by week 10–12.
- Functional checks before on-snow return: pain-free single-leg squat to at least a controlled 70–80° knee angle (pain-free), single-leg hop test is normally used for return but because of no jumping restriction, perform controlled single-leg hop simulation on soft surface or step-downs under load — consult surgeon/physio.
- Clearance: final clearance from surgeon/physio recommended prior to resuming dynamic on-snow activities.

Nutrition & supplementation guidance (general — personalize as needed)
- Calories: For strength gain, aim for a modest surplus of ~+200–300 kcal/day if client wants to gain muscle; if they prefer to maintain weight, shoot for maintenance calories.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (0.7–1.0 g/lb). Spread protein across 3–4 meals, include 20–40 g protein per meal.
- Carbohydrate: 3–5 g/kg/day tailored to training volume — higher on heavy training days to support intensity (pre/post-workout carbs help performance).
- Fat: 20–30% of calories from healthy fats.
- Supplements: Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (supports strength gains and recovery). Vitamin D if deficient. Omega-3 (1–2 g EPA+DHA/day) can help inflammation management.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day baseline; more around training.

Recovery & soft tissue
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly.
- Post-session: if joint twinges or swelling, use RICE as needed (rest, ice 10–15 min, compression, elevation), and reduce next session intensity/volume.
- Use compression sleeves for knee if they help the client feel stable during sessions.
- Schedule regular soft-tissue work, foam rolling and mobility work 3–5x/week.

If things go wrong (pain, swelling, locking)
- Immediate protocol: stop activity, rest, apply ice and compression, and contact surgeon/physio if swelling is new or locking/catching occurs. Avoid accelerating the program until cleared.

Sample 12-week micro-progression summary
- Weeks 1–3: Build technique and tolerance (3–4 x 6–12 rep ranges). Week 4 = deload.
- Weeks 5–7: Increase intensity; heavier sets 4–6 reps, more single-leg load. Week 8 = deload.
- Weeks 9–11: Heavier main lifts 3–5 reps, more force/velocity training via sleds and med ball (no jumps). Week 12: managed peak and functional testing before on-snow training.

Notes for you as trainer
- Use objective measures: single-leg RDL load, trap-bar 3RM, and sled push times to monitor progress.
- Adjust exercise selection if knee tolerance varies — e.g., swap Bulgarian split squat for single-leg RDL or reverse lunge for single-leg pressing if front knee pain occurs.
- Emphasize neuromuscular control for deceleration (eccentric training) — crucial for safe skiing.

If you’d like I can:
- Convert this to printable week-by-week tables with exact loads per week (e.g., % of 1RM) if you have his current 1RMs.
- Provide a more conservative or more aggressive progression depending on his current pain/tolerance and lifting history.
- Create a pre-ski 2-week on-snow transition plan (gradual reintroduction of dynamic tasks) once you have surgeon/physio sign-off.

Would you like the program laid out in a printable daily sheet for each of the 12 weeks or do you want me to tailor sets and percentages if you can share his current 1RMs and baseline single-leg performance?
